title: Initial embodied steering from the frozen MaleCNS visual circuit
question: Does the validated MaleCNS-derived visual-motion signal drive a different steering response when the same two-column motion order is reversed?

preserved_history.EXP-001: unchanged strict-LIF baseline; L1 responded, Mi1/Tm3 was subthreshold, and T4 did not spike
preserved_history.EXP-002: unchanged and frozen graded local T4 direction-selectivity experiment
preserved_history.technical_diagnostics: Brian2/NumPy and MaleCNS annotation diagnostics remain provenance records, not biological experiments

model.downstream_dynamics: instantaneous synapse-count-normalized linear T4-to-wide-field-to-descending readout; not interpreted as downstream membrane voltage

body_layer.controller: FlyGym HybridTurningFly with its existing low-level CPG and contact rules
body_layer.closed_loop_visual_transform: fly yaw shifts the timing of the two-column retinal pulses by 100 ms per radian
body_layer.geometry_status: The MaleCNS workbook suffix-to-visual-axis mapping is unresolved; conditions are named forward/reverse order only, not front/back or left/right.

temporary_motor_bridge.biological_input: descending activity from the materialized MaleCNS downstream graph
temporary_motor_bridge.readout: normalized path mass from T4a-dominant descending targets minus T4d-dominant descending targets
temporary_motor_bridge.status: explicit artificial actuator bridge; fixed before the final run; not learned and not a direct stimulus-direction lookup

control.name: T4-to-wide-field projection ablation
control.operation: remove all selected T4-to-wide-field matrix entries before descending readout
control.purpose: test whether steering disappears when the relevant MaleCNS downstream path is disconnected

result.interpretation: The embodied system turns differently in magnitude when order is reversed, and the difference disappears under T4-to-wide-field ablation. It does not yet produce opposite-signed turns, so the EXP-003 qualitative success criterion is not fully met.
